alerts.title: EFV neuropsychiatric toxicity: insomnia and vivid dreams
alerts.message: Guidelines state EFV frequently causes neuropsychiatric effects including insomnia, vivid dreams, and dizziness, typically within the first 2-6 weeks of therapy. The patient has been on EFV since February 2024 and now presents with poor sleep and vivid dreams for several weeks. While most EFV neuropsychiatric effects occur early, persistent or late-presenting symptoms are recognised. Evidence for drug attribution: the symptoms match the classic EFV neuropsychiatric profile. Evidence against: the onset is nearly 2 years after EFV initiation, whereas guidelines note most cases occur within 2-6 weeks. The clinician's plan documents the complaints but does not propose any management action.

evidence.recommended_action: Assess symptom severity and consider EFV substitution if persistent CNS toxicity. Screen for depression and suicidality using validated tools. Submit aDSM form to NDA.

alerts.title: Missing baseline and monitoring labs
alerts.message: No renal function, hepatic function, or haematology results are recorded for this patient on TDF/3TC/EFV. TDF requires renal monitoring and EFV requires hepatic monitoring per guidelines. The only lab on record is a viral load from August 2025 showing 60 copies/mL. The clinician's plan does not include any laboratory orders.

evidence.recommended_action: Order renal function (creatinine/eGFR), hepatic function (ALT/AST), and haematology labs to monitor TDF and EFV toxicity.

alerts.title: Plan lacks management for EFV CNS symptoms
alerts.message: The clinician's plan documents insomnia and vivid dreams but does not include any diagnostic or therapeutic action. Guidelines list persistent CNS toxicity and mental symptoms such as anxiety and depression as major adverse events of EFV requiring management. The plan also does not include screening for depression or suicidality, which guidelines identify as a common concern requiring additional assessment.

evidence.recommended_action: Develop a management plan: assess severity, screen for depression/suicidality with validated tools (PHQ-9), and consider EFV substitution if symptoms persist.
